messages.author: 8f7bc2739b78be4d
messages.subject: Omitting values from legend
parts:
I have a variable --pause-- with values 0,1,3,5, that I'm using for point sizes, but the legend shows point symbols for 2,4 that aren't in the graph. How can I omit those?

ggplot(e,aes(id, rate,colour=flow))
p + geom_point(aes(size=pause),legend_param=list(e$pause)) + ylab("rate(%)") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(55,100)) + opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(colour = "#000000", face = "bold"), axis.title.y = theme_text(face="bold"))

Thanks for any advice.

Tony Bigbee

messages.subject: Re: Omitting values from legend
parts:
Hi Tony,

Looks like Brandon's suggestion might help. If you convert it from
continuous to factor, you will just get the discrete sizes.
Alternately, if you still wanted to specify particular breaks, you
would need to switch from scale_size_discrete to scale_size_continuous
since it is integer class, not discrete right now.

HTH,

Josh

messages.subject: Re: Omitting values from legend
parts:
Well, if you want proportionality, you are basically talking about a
continuous variable at which point, you can just customize particular
break points and labels (as with scale_size_continuous()) rather than
factor()ing. factor() is just a convenient way to numerify (submitted
to the OED, but rejected ;) categorical data (or in Tony's case,
"drop" from the legend unused numerical entries by converting 0, 1, 3,
5 to 1, 2, 3, 4 esentially (the underlying numeric frame of the
factor).

Josh
